content_note: Every rule here is intent-only: a name, an id and a logic line that names the detections the rule would join. There is no query, schedule, severity or alert mapping, so nothing in this file can be imported into a tenant as-is. Author the rule in the XSIAM console from the logic line.

rules.logic:
Operator-installed correlation rule (CortexSim never writes it to the tenant). Install it as follows. Alert name EXACTLY as this rule's name. Severity Medium (only Medium or higher opens or joins a case). Scheduled, every 10 minutes, query time frame 1 hour. Alert suppression on: one issue per agent per hour (suppression duration 1 hour, suppression field agent_id), so one burst raises one issue and not one on each of the six scheduled runs that still see it. Alert field mapping: agent_hostname -> Host Name, agent_id -> Agent ID (the mapped artifacts are what let a correlation issue join a case). MITRE mapping: leave it EMPTY while SIM-EDR-028 is being scored, even though the generated export file for this card lists MITRE techniques beside the rule. Every row of a step shares the step's technique, so an issue tagged T1068 would also be credited to the XQL validation rows of step-02. Outside a scored run the natural tag is T1068. TESTED AS A QUERY, NOT AS A RULE. On 2026-11-14 the XQL below was run in the lab tenant as an ordinary query over a one-hour time frame. At 01:34 UTC, before any run that hour, it was accepted and returned 0 rows. At 01:56 UTC, after SIM-EDR-028 run 5c500f71 (01:42:44 to 01:45:06), it was accepted and returned one row for pov-target-01 with sudoedit_starts 44: that run's 28 recorded starts plus about 16 from an earlier attempt in the same hour, run 328b3e45 at 01:39:56, which was cut off in step-02 after 55 s. SimCore had answered one of the beacon's control polls with HTTP 500 ('database is locked', while another client's tenant call held the database), and the beacon treated that as an abort: a SimCore defect being fixed separately, not a fault of this scenario. The rule has not been installed (no tenant write was made), so it has not run on a schedule, has raised no issue, and its suppression setting has not been exercised. Its comp-then-filter shape follows CR-EDR-0023, which was tested read-only in the lab tenant on 2026-11-11. It reads only process-start events, the one kind SIM-EDR-028 step-02 produces sixty times on one host, and it matches the command line, not the image name, because sudoedit is normally a symbolic link to sudo and the sensor may report the image as sudo. It fires for an endpoint with 20 or more sudoedit -s process starts inside the rule's one-hour time frame. Its output is the two host fields and the count. There is no _time column and no time bucket, so nothing in the row can date the issue before the run that caused it: which timestamp an issue carries is an open question in this repository, and a result match is accepted only at or after the launch. The count of 20 is this scenario's choice: the alert page publishes no threshold. In run 5c500f71 the agent recorded 28 of the sixty starts (the first 28, then none; cause not established), so the floor held. On a host whose agent records fewer than 20 of the sixty the rule does not fire; the read-back query on this card is how to check. There is no current_time in the rule: the time frame bounds it. XQL:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_command_line ~= "(^|/)sudoedit +-s( |$)"
| comp count() as sudoedit_starts by agent_hostname, agent_id
| filter sudoedit_starts >= 20
rules.name: EDR-028 Sudoedit Execution Burst On One Host
